document_name: Nidec Motor Manual.pdf
question: According to the Nidec U.S. MOTORS product service manual, what must the inspection of a motor after extended storage include?
answer: An external inspection (unit clean, ventilation openings clear, no damage); a megger test of the windings for insulation resistance; rotating the shaft to check for bearing roughness or rubbing; a bench test for excessive amp draw, noise or vibration; regreasing the bearings as applicable; and a plate/tag with the inspection date, installed by an authorized service station
source: Motor Inspection Procedure After Storage, p.20

document_name: Nidec Motor Manual.pdf
question: Why can a U.S. MOTORS brand motor ordered with class F insulation arrive with a class B nameplate?
answer: All motors are built with class F insulation or better; a class B nameplate means the motor is designed to stay within class B temperature rise limits (80 °C at 1.0 service factor, 90 °C at 1.15) — open dripproof motors meeting that are nameplated B regardless of the actual insulation
source: Class B vs. Class F Insulation, p.20

document_name: Nidec Motor Manual.pdf
question: How is the rotation of a U.S. MOTORS brand TEFC motor with a sirocco-type fan reversed in the field?
answer: Remove the fan cover guard and the fan (heating the hub if needed); move the baffle plate to the opposite side of the fan casting (drilling and tapping new holes, using the plate as a template); re-balance the fan; reinstall it with the baffle plate toward the motor; refit the guard; turn the rotation arrows 180 degrees; reverse the leads if required. Propeller fans need a different fan; radial fans are bi-directional
source: Reversing Direction of Rotation on TEFC Motors, p.21

question: On a U.S. MOTORS vertical motor with spring-loaded spherical roller or angular contact thrust bearings, what end play must be set, and how long may the motor run without load?
answer: An end play of .005 to .008 inches; the motor must not run without load for more than fifteen minutes, or the lower bearing may be damaged and improper seating of the thrust bearing may cause vibration

question: According to the Nidec manual, what causes the lubricating oil of a vertical motor to foam, and how is it corrected?
answer: Moisture contamination, cleaning solvents and similar contaminants in the oil (milky appearance, bubbles dissipating slowly); steam-clean and bake dry the oil reservoir and associated parts so all contaminants and moisture are removed; if it persists, add an anti-foaming agent
